description: Cucumis sativus: a climbing, tendrilled annual.

diseases.name: Angular Leaf Spot
diseases.description: A bacterial leaf spot of cucumber with angular, vein-bounded spots that tear out.
diseases.causes: Bacteria come in on seed and spread by rain splash, handling and insects in warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Small, water-soaked, angular spots bounded by the veins
A milky ooze on the spots in humid mornings
Spots dry, turn tan and fall out, leaving ragged holes
diseases.effect: Leaves are ragged; fruit can be spotted and rot.

steps.title: Remove spotted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off spotted leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Stay out of wet plants
steps.instruction: Do not handle plants while wet.

steps.title: Copper spray where advised
steps.instruction: Spray a registered copper product following the label.

lifecycle: Bacteria come in on seed or debris.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: cucumber angular leaf spot

diseases.name: Bacterial Wilt
diseases.description: A bacterial disease that blocks the water vessels of cucumber, so the vines wilt and die.
diseases.causes: Striped and spotted cucumber beetles carry the bacteria in their gut and infect plants as they feed.
symptoms: Single leaves wilt and look dull green
Whole runners, then the plant, wilt and do not recover overnight
Cut stems ooze sticky threads when pulled apart
diseases.effect: Wilted plants die within one to two weeks.
diseases.untreated: Beetles keep spreading the bacteria to the rest of the planting.

steps.title: Remove wilted plants
steps.instruction: Pull out and remove wilted plants at once.
steps.rationale: They are a source for the beetles.

steps.title: Control cucumber beetles
steps.instruction: Check plants daily, hand-pick or use netting, and use controls registered locally.

steps.title: Cover young plants
steps.instruction: Use insect netting until flowering (open it for pollinators).
steps.rationale: Young plants are most at risk.

lifecycle: The bacteria overwinter inside cucumber beetles.
Leaves, then the whole plant, wilt and die.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: cucumber bacterial wilt
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Powdery Mildew
diseases.description: A fungal disease that coats cucumber leaves with white powder.
diseases.causes: Spores blow in on the wind; warm days, shade and dense plants favour it, and the leaves need not be wet.
symptoms: White, powdery spots on both sides of the leaves
Spots spread to cover the leaf
diseases.effect: Fewer leaves means smaller, poorer fruit.

steps.title: Remove the worst leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off the worst leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Improve airflow and light
steps.rationale: Shade and still air favour it.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray sulphur or another registered product on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: Spores blow in from other cucurbits.
conditions: Older leaves later in the season.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: cucumber powdery mildew
